page: Google Cloud Platform m1-megamem-96 is a memory-optimized cloud server engineered for massive in-memory architectures. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon processor providing 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled. The configuration includes 38 MB of shared L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache, supplemented by instruction set extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA. Its defining feature is a 1434.0 GB memory capacity, equivalent to approximately 14.93 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached volumes, and operates without discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture oriented toward parallel throughput and substantial memory capacity rather than raw single-core frequency. In multi-threaded execution, the server shows strong performance, reaching 70,552.79 in stress-ng multi-core and 49,280.55 in PassMark CPU tests, accompanied by a strong Clang compilation score of 38,951.0. Memory bandwidth exhibits high read throughput, measuring 3,918.5 GB/sec on cached 16 KB blocks and 201.93 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads. In contrast, single-thread metrics fall in the lower quartile, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,026.0 and stress-ng single-core output of 1,273.18. Uncached 256 MB writes place in the middle tier at 89.97 GB/sec, matching its average Geekbench multi-core result of 10,625.0.

From an infrastructure and cost efficiency perspective, m1-megamem-96 concentrates capital investment into its extensive 1.4 TB memory footprint and dedicated compute allocation. Because single-thread performance is modest and sequential compression tasks execute at lower relative speeds, it is poorly suited for compute-heavy or single-threaded workloads. Instead, the server delivers balanced multi-core density, handling up to 60.51 million Redis SET operations per second and 37.02 GB/sec in static web serving. The hardware is best matched for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale data analytics caching, and massive multi-threaded backend processing pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform m1-megamem-96 is a memory-optimized virtual machine delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor. Designed for data-intensive infrastructure, it features 1434.0 GB of system memory, an L3 cache of 38 MB, and support for AVX-512F extensions. The instance excludes discrete GPUs and local storage, relying on network-attached storage architectures. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate high multi-core throughput, recording 70,552.79 on stress-ng multi-core and strong uncached read bandwidth of 201.93 GB/sec. Conversely, single-thread performance ranks in the lower quartile, visible in a Geekbench single-core score of 1,026.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 21.69 GB/sec. In application benchmarks, it manages 60.51 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance is suited for large in-memory databases, real-time caching, and high-concurrency enterprise workloads requiring vast memory capacity.
